note: Declares what .github/workflows/202609042220-promotion-lane-build.yml (the build lane) and .github/workflows/202609042220-promotion-lane-promote.yml (the promotion lane) actually do. Checked against vaccines/202609032337-promotion-authority-separated.md in Ventusltd/cvaa. gridatlas serves main directly to GitHub Pages (classic Pages, no build step), so 'promote' here means exactly one thing: fast-forwarding refs/heads/main to a commit that has already been proved.

build.branch_only_evidence: triggers are 'push: branches: ["candidate/**"]' and 'pull_request:' only — no 'push: branches: [main]' and no 'workflow_dispatch' that could target main.
build.permissions_evidence: job-level 'permissions: contents: read' is the only permission block in the file; there is no 'contents: write', no 'pages: write', no 'id-token: write'.
build.may_promote_evidence: the workflow has no step that runs 'git push', 'gh api .../pages/builds', or touches refs/heads/main; its last step uploads a JSON proof receipt as a workflow artifact and writes it to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. It cannot write to the repository and cannot dispatch the promotion lane.

promotion.explicit_dispatch_evidence: the only trigger is 'workflow_dispatch', with two required inputs, 'generation' and 'proof_run_id'; there is no push, schedule, or pull_request trigger.
promotion.authority_evidence: the job runs as the named principal 'gridatlas-release-authority' (git author identity of the promotion commit; the actual invoking GitHub identity is the account or App that owns the token in the GRIDATLAS_PROMOTION_TOKEN secret, which is the only credential this lane accepts, checked at the top of the job) — a build-lane run has no access to this secret and no dispatch trigger that could reach this workflow.
promotion.may_push_main_evidence: the job's 'permissions: contents: write' is declared ONLY on this workflow, never on the build lane, and only this workflow contains a step that runs 'git push origin <commit>:refs/heads/main'.
